name: Current: Durum wheat - Sunflower
why: This is what the field grows today. It is the baseline the other options are compared against.

evidence.fact: [MOCK] Placeholder: summer maximum temperatures often above 35 °C during sunflower flowering.
[MOCK] Placeholder: heaviest rain weeks fall in autumn, when the soil is still bare.

risks: Soil left bare from July to October

name: A: Durum wheat - Chickpea
why: A legume replaces sunflower: it adds nitrogen to the soil and uses less water in summer.

evidence.fact: [MOCK] Placeholder: spring rainfall usually covers chickpea needs in an average year.
[MOCK] Placeholder: soil moisture is currently below normal for November.

benefits: Less nitrogen fertiliser for the next wheat
risks: Chickpea is sensitive to heat at flowering

name: B: Barley - Vetch - Durum wheat
why: A three-year cycle with a vetch year that covers the soil and rebuilds organic matter.

evidence.fact: [MOCK] Placeholder: autumn heavy-rain weeks coincide with vetch ground cover.
[MOCK] Placeholder: barley ripens before the hottest weeks of the year.

benefits: Barley avoids the worst summer heat
gaps: Forage demand and price not checked
risks: Lower income in the vetch year
Needs a buyer or use for the forage

name: C: Wheat - Sunflower - Chickpea + cover crop
why: Keeps the familiar crops but adds a legume and a cover crop so the soil is never bare in autumn.

evidence.fact: [MOCK] Placeholder: a cover crop would protect the soil during the autumn heavy-rain peak.
[MOCK] Placeholder: dry autumn soils may delay cover crop establishment.

benefits: Familiar crops stay in the plan
gaps: Cover crop seed cost not included
Few local trials in rainfed soils
risks: Cover crop may fail in a dry autumn
